meta.description: Single source of truth for the Steins;Gate explainer app. Every story fact carries sourceIds (resolving to the sources array) and a confidence tag. All text is paraphrased from research notes; no script text. Built from six research-notes files; see research/sources.md and research/canon-notes.md.

confidenceLevels.CONFIRMED: Stated as canon by a reference source that cites the VN, anime or an official guidebook, or backed by two or more independent sources. If all support comes from one site, the object carries singleSource: true (singleSourceKind 'fan_wiki' => UI shows 'per fan wiki').
confidenceLevels.INTERPRETATION: A fan or analyst reading, an inference by the researchers, or (by the characters notes' convention) a factual claim from a single fan-wiki page that the researcher declined to promote. Display as a reading, not a fact.
confidenceLevels.UNCLEAR: Sources conflict, the only source is weak, or the claim is unverified. Always show competing versions from disputes/conflicts when available.

fieldConventions.confidence: Confidence that the event/fact happened or holds.
fieldConventions.dateConfidence: Confidence in the calendar date specifically (events).
fieldConventions.divergenceConfidence: Confidence in the exact digits of a world line.
fieldConventions.sortDate: Ordering key; if sortDateIsEditorial is true it is NOT a story fact and must never be displayed as a date.
fieldConventions.seq: Okabe's subjective order. Main story 1-37; original-VN ending branches 150+; Steins;Gate 0 lane 200+.
fieldConventions.reveals: Additional facts about the parent object that unlock at a higher spoilerTier. Never render a reveal below its tier (including tooltips, alt text, titles, URLs).
fieldConventions.lane: Map lane: sg_main, steins_gate, sg_vn_ending, sg0, spinoff.
fieldConventions.media: Which works show this fact or value (see mediaKeys).

spoilerTiers.label: Premise only (spoiler-safe)
spoilerTiers.covers: VN Prologue-Ch 01 / anime eps 1-2: July 28, the first D-Mail, discovering the phone-microwave. Generic mechanics (world line, divergence, D-Mail, Reading Steiner).

spoilerTiers.label: Steins;Gate part 1
spoilerTiers.covers: Up to the raid: D-Mail experiments, SERN hack, IBN 5100 (VN to ~Ch 04-05 / anime eps 3-11).

spoilerTiers.label: Steins;Gate part 2
spoilerTiers.covers: Raid, time leaps, Titor reveal, attractor fields, undoing D-Mails (VN ~Ch 05-09 / anime eps 12-21).

spoilerTiers.label: Steins;Gate ending
spoilerTiers.covers: Beta return, Operation Skuld, Steins Gate line, all original VN endings (VN Ch 10-11 / anime eps 22-24, OVA).

spoilerTiers.label: Steins;Gate 0
spoilerTiers.covers: Ep 23-beta and all Steins;Gate 0 content (spoils the original's ending).

spoilerTiers.label: Extras
spoilerTiers.covers: Film, spin-offs, novels, Re:Boot Gamma route, spin-off world lines.

decisions: Opening line: 1.130426% (VN on-screen value, three sources) is the canonical display value; 1.130246% (script) and 1.129848% (Fandom Timeline label) are stored as alternateValues; divergenceConfidence UNCLEAR. 1.130205% is the Ch 10 / ep 22 return line, not the start; the two Beta nodes are never merged.

When notes give different tags to the same claim, canon.json uses the weaker tag, unless the notes jointly cite two independent sources (e.g. Fandom + wiki.gg), in which case it is CONFIRMED with both listed.

Single-source convention: a CONFIRMED object whose sourceIds all come from one site gets singleSource: true (kind fan_wiki / wikipedia / other) so the UI can show 'per fan wiki'. Two Fandom pages count as one site.

Calendar dates sourced only to Fandom (D-Mail table + Timeline) get dateConfidence UNCLEAR even though the event and its order are CONFIRMED (order rests on wiki.gg chapter mapping and Wikipedia episode summaries).

Events carry both calendar order (array order by sortDate/time) and Okabe's subjective order (seq). The July 28 rescue attempts sit on July 28 in calendar mode but at seq 31/35; the Aug 11 failed Moeka cancellation sits at seq 24, after the Aug 15 Luka cancellation.
Events without a sourced date get date null and an editorial sortDate (sortDateIsEditorial: true), which must never be displayed.

Steins;Gate 0 forks from world line 1.130209% (after the first time-machine trip) to 1.129848% via tr-sg0-branch, tagged INTERPRETATION, as the notes infer from ep 23-beta promo material showing both values.

No synthetic transitions: where a media filter hides an intermediate line (e.g. anime viewers never see 1.130209/1.130212), the UI collapses consecutive edges into one dashed 'collapsed' edge. S;G 0 VN route links are only drawn where the notes state 'after X' with a known predecessor; other S;G 0 nodes float in the S;G 0 lane.
Steins Gate (1.048596%) gets attractorField 'steins_gate' and its own lane; whether it is a separate field is recorded as dispute dsp-sg-line-status.

Spin-off, novel, manga and Re:Boot-only values are kept but tagged media 'other' and tier 'extras' so the UI can hide them by default. -0.275349 is stored once, tagged vn+other, UNCLEAR, because sources disagree whether it is the VN Faris ending or a spin-off Omega line.
All original VN branch endings are gated at sg_ending even though some branch mid-story, because each reveals late-story outcomes.

Generic mechanics (world line, divergence, D-Mail, Reading Steiner, Divergence Meter display) are premise tier; anything naming who/when (meter from 2036, Titor = Suzuha, FB = Yugo) is a higher-tier 'reveal'.
Character aliases, relationships, fates and reveals carry their own spoilerTier (e.g. Suzuha's 'John Titor' alias is sg_part2).
Lab Mem numbers: 001-003, 005, 007, 008 CONFIRMED; 004 Kurisu and 006 Luka INTERPRETATION (join order); 010 Kagari INTERPRETATION; 009/011 unknown (null).
Real-world John Titor and in-story Titor are separate glossary entries; the real-world one is marked realWorld: true.

Pages that failed or returned wrong content are kept in sources with status flags; 'failed' and 'search-only' sources are never cited by any fact. 'wrong-content' sources are cited only for what their returned text actually contained.
Endings whose world line is inferred (Suzuha, Luka) carry worldLineConfidence INTERPRETATION.

characters.name: Rintaro Okabe
characters.role: Founder of the Future Gadget Laboratory in Akihabara and a self-proclaimed mad scientist whose persona is largely a facade; a university student. The story is told from his point of view.

relationships.type: friend and fellow Lab member (fan wikis disagree on whether they attended the same high school)
fellow Lab member; he calls her 'Assistant' and 'Christina'

readingSteiner.notes: Okabe's own name for his ability to keep his memories when the world line changes. Others' memories are rewritten; his carry over. He does not feel it during time leaps. Its origin is never explained; a childhood fever around age 8 is implied.

alpha.text: In the Alpha future he and Daru co-found a resistance, and Okabe is killed by SERN's Rounders in 2025.
alpha.note: Each wiki was tagged single-source in a different notes file; together they meet the two-independent-source rule.

beta.text: In one Beta future shown in Steins;Gate 0 (anime ep 20), Okabe is captured in 2025 and is brain-dead by 2036.

steinsGate.text: Reaches the Steins Gate world line (1.048596%) and saves Kurisu; he is hospitalized after being stabbed, then reunites with her in Akihabara.

sg0.text: Abandons the Hououin Kyouma persona and suffers guilt and panic attacks, later regaining his drive. In 2025 he sends a video D-Mail to his past self and leaves in a time machine to rescue Mayuri and Suzuha.

characters.name: Kurisu Makise

labMemberNumber.note: Inferred from the Lab's join order; her own wiki page states no number.

characters.role: Neuroscience researcher at Viktor Chondria University's Brain Science Institute and the story's main heroine. Her age is given inconsistently across sources.

relationships.type: friend and junior colleague (Maho is her senior)

readingSteiner.notes: On the Steins Gate line she briefly and involuntarily recalls Alpha-line memories mid-conversation; in the 2013 film she relies on this deja vu.

alpha.text: Alive in 2010 on the Alpha lines: she joins the Lab and builds the Time Leap Machine.

details.text: In the Alpha future SERN takes her hostage in 2011 and forces her to work in Geneva.

beta.text: Dies on July 28, 2010 at Radio Kaikan.

details.text: When Okabe travels back to save her, he accidentally stabs her himself while trying to stop her father.

steinsGate.text: Survives; reunites with Okabe in Akihabara and seems to remember other world lines.

sg0.text: Dead on this line; her memory data lives on in the Amadeus AI, and her laptop and thesis are fought over by rival factions.

reveals.text: She builds the Time Leap Machine, which sends memories up to 48 hours into the past.

characters.name: Mayuri Shiina
characters.role: Okabe's childhood friend and Lab Mem 002; works part-time at the MayQueen NyanNyan maid cafe; catchphrase 'Tutturu~'. As a child, after her grandmother died, Okabe declared her his 'hostage' to pull her out of depression.

relationships.type: adoptive mother (met 2028, adopted 2032 per one page; another page says 2036)

readingSteiner.notes: On world line 0.571046% she remembers her many deaths as nightmares.

alpha.text: Dies on every Alpha line by convergence: shot in the Rounders' raid, and after each time leap by other means (run over, pushed onto train tracks).

sg0.text: Survives; later adopts the war orphan Kagari. In the anime she ends up stranded in 18,000 BC with Suzuha until Okabe rescues them.

characters.name: Itaru Hashida
characters.role: Lab Mem 003 and Okabe's friend; a hacker skilled in both software and hardware.

alpha.text: In the Alpha future he builds the time machine Suzuha uses, co-founds a resistance with Okabe, and is killed by Rounders in 2033.

sg0.text: In 2025 he sends the D-Mail carrying the Operation Arc Light plan to Suzuha and Mayuri; with Maho he rebuilds the Time Leap Machine.

reveals.text: He is Suzuha's future father and the builder of her time machine (signed 'Barrel Titor').

travelled from 2036 with her; lost her in 1998

sg0.text: Stays on the Beta line after the failed rescue; her time machine is destroyed by a DURPA missile (anime ep 19), and she is stranded with Mayuri in 18,000 BC until Okabe rescues them.

details.text: Pretends to be Daru's sister and searches for Kagari.

reveals.text: She is a time traveller from 2036, Daru's future daughter, who posts online as 'John Titor'.

glossary.plainLanguage: One complete version of history. Only one world line is 'active' at a time; the others exist only as possibilities, not as parallel universes.
glossary.details: When the world 'transfers' to a different world line, the old one disappears. The series frames this through an in-universe 'Attractor Field Theory'.

glossary.plainLanguage: Each world line has a number, shown as a percentage with six decimal places (for example 0.571024%). Think of it as the world line's address.
glossary.details: What the number is measured against is never firmly defined: one wiki calls it a 'percent difference from the original world line', another says the meter measures local gravitational variation. Undoing a change lands on a nearby, not identical, number (0.409420% versus 0.409431%). The first digit usually names the attractor field, but this is only a rule of thumb.

glossary.plainLanguage: A bundle of world lines that, despite small differences, all lead to the same key outcome. Small changes inside a field cannot escape that outcome.
glossary.details: Minor changes that keep the same result are ineffective; only a drastic change beyond the field's range (a 'Major Divergence') breaks the fixed fate. Sources frame convergence differently: as probability (Fandom) or as the world preventing change 'by any means possible' (wiki.gg).

glossary.plainLanguage: Within one attractor field, history keeps arriving at the same outcome. You can change when or how something happens, but not whether it happens.
glossary.details: On screen: after one D-Mail is undone, Mayuri still dies, just a day later (anime ep 17); when Okabe tries to take a car's impact, Mayuri pushes him aside and dies instead (ep 21).

glossary.plainLanguage: The family of world lines numbered 0.x%. On every one of them Mayuri dies in August 2010, and SERN later rules the world.
glossary.details: Fandom's range is 0.000000 to 'presumably' 0.999999. Long-term outcome: SERN completes a time machine and humanity is ruled by SERN and the Committee of 300 by 2036. The anime has Suzuha attribute Mayuri's doomed fate to the convergence of the Alpha field (ep 14).

glossary.plainLanguage: The family of world lines numbered 1.x%. Mayuri lives, but Kurisu dies on July 28, 2010 and the world heads toward World War III.
glossary.details: Nakabachi escapes to Russia with Kurisu's time-machine thesis, triggering a time-machine arms race and World War III. Most of Steins;Gate 0 takes place in the Beta field.

glossary.plainLanguage: To leave the Alpha family (0.x%) for the Beta family (1.x%), the divergence has to cross 1%. Small tweaks are not enough.
glossary.details: Titor tells Okabe he may be able to lead the world beyond the '1% divergence' point (anime ep 7); Suzuha says he must cross it (ep 14). A '2% barrier' is not in any reference source, and a physicist's blog figure of '4%' is contradicted by all other sources. No source explains why the boundaries fall on whole percentages.

reveals.text: Okabe actually crosses it by undoing every D-Mail and then erasing the record of his first D-Mail from SERN's database.

glossary.plainLanguage: The final world line, 1.048596%, where neither Alpha's nor Beta's fixed outcome happens: both Mayuri and Kurisu live and there is no World War III or SERN dystopia.
glossary.details: Sources disagree on whether it is 'between' the fields, 'under the influence of both', or 'an independent attractor field'; official guidebooks list it without a field symbol. The number is reportedly a creator pun (0 Okabe, 4 Shiina, 8 Hashida, 596 'gokuro', roughly 'good work'), a single-sourced claim.

glossary.plainLanguage: A Nixie-tube gadget that shows the current world line's number to six decimal places. Only someone who remembers the previous reading can tell that it changed.
glossary.details: Changes beyond the sixth decimal are not registered; it cannot show negative values (the first digit is left blank). It only became meaningful for Okabe because a world-line change rewrites everyone else's memory of the previous reading. Invention year is disputed (2021 vs 'some years before 2020'); no source ties it to 2025.

reveals.text: Suzuha brought it from 2036 and gives it to Okabe (anime ep 15); it was invented by a future Okabe and passed to Daru, then to Suzuha.

glossary.plainLanguage: Okabe's name for his ability to keep his memories when the world line changes. Everyone else's memories quietly rewrite themselves to match the new history; his do not.
glossary.details: It fires when a D-Mail or a present-day action causes a measurable change. Sensation: vertigo, the world going monochrome and twisting for a few seconds. It does not fire for changes too small to move the meter, for physical time travellers, or for time leaps. Others show weaker forms (deja vu, dreams). Okabe names it in anime ep 8.

glossary.plainLanguage: A short text message sent into the past with the Lab's modified microwave. If it changes what someone does, the world line shifts.
glossary.details: Limited to about 36 bytes, sent as three 12-byte pieces (about 36 English or 18 Japanese characters); the excess is lost. The microwave timer sets how far back it goes, in one-hour steps. No hard maximum reach is stated; sends to January 1993 and April 3, 2000 occur. Naming per a single fan wiki: in the VN Daru coins 'DeLorean Mail', in the anime Mayuri proposes the name, and Kurisu shortens it to 'D-Mail'; Wikipedia credits only 'the group' (anime ep 6).

glossary.plainLanguage: The Lab's accidental time machine: a microwave oven with a cell phone wired into it. It can send text messages into the past.
glossary.details: Started by calling the attached phone, which plays a recorded voice guide by Mayuri, then pressing '#' and entering a duration in seconds (single wiki). Microwave specs 2.45 GHz and about 1,500-2,000 W (single wiki). Which member physically built it is not stated in the notes.

glossary.plainLanguage: The microwave only sends messages while a big CRT television in the shop downstairs is switched on. It supplies the electrons the effect needs.
glossary.details: When Yugo switched off his CRT during tremors, the effect stopped at once (anime ep 11). The wiki calls it a 42-inch CRT (a translation of the Japanese size term). SERN uses a comparable 'lifter' to inject electrons and control its black holes.

glossary.plainLanguage: The series' in-universe science: the microwave accidentally makes tiny spinning black holes, and data can slip through them into the past.
glossary.details: In the VN, Daru describes SERN's LHC and Kurisu explains that the microwave and phone waves accelerate particles like an accelerator. In 'Titor's theory', mini black holes become rotating Kerr black holes with a ring singularity; with enough spin the event horizon vanishes, leaving a 'naked singularity' that can be passed through. Anime eps 11-12 titles reference 'Event Horizon' and 'Ergosphere'; whether the anime contains the full explanation is unverified.

glossary.plainLanguage: Objects put through the microwave come back as green gel: the first clue that it does something strange. A banana even reappears back on its bunch, as gel.
glossary.details: Matter too large for the passage is crushed by 'supergravity' and comes out as gel (single wiki); a frozen 'Juicy Chicken Number One' gelled too. SERN's past human time-travel tests killed the subjects the same way.

glossary.plainLanguage: Kurisu's upgrade to the microwave that sends a person's memories, not their body, back to their own past self, up to 48 hours earlier.
glossary.details: A headset digitizes memories, the hacked SERN LHC compresses them to D-Mail size, and the data arrives at the leaper's own phone in the past; the past self must answer and hold the phone to their ear. 48 hours is the safe limit (a longer jump risks brain damage, single wiki). In Steins;Gate 0, Maho extends it to two weeks.

glossary.plainLanguage: A real, person-carrying time machine from 2036. Unlike the microwave, it moves bodies, not just data.
glossary.details: It controls Kerr black holes, uses fuel from a car-battery-sized cell each trip, and each trip nudges the divergence slightly (two Beta trips: 1.130209% then 1.130212%). The Alpha-line model is one-way to the past. It sits wedged on the roof of Radio Kaikan. Designations FG204 / C204 / C203 / C193 / OR204 are reported inconsistently.

glossary.plainLanguage: A rare 1975 computer. It can read an old programming language that SERN's database still uses, which makes it the key to hacking SERN.
glossary.details: Modelled on the real IBM 5100. On the Beta field it is donated to Yanabayashi Shrine after Faris's father dies; on Alpha lines where he lives, he sells it. Moeka's D-Mail makes her take it from the shrine first. Specs (about 25 kg, all-in-one) are single wiki.

glossary.plainLanguage: A fictional, sinister version of the real research centre CERN, secretly chasing time travel.
glossary.details: Based in Meyrin, Geneva, founded 1954, secretly controlled by the Committee of 300. It watches communications through ECHELON, which is how it detects the Lab's D-Mails. Its past human time-travel attempts killed the test subjects.

glossary.plainLanguage: A hidden group that secretly controls SERN; the central antagonist group of the wider Science Adventure series.
glossary.details: Details beyond 'controls SERN' could not be researched (the Fandom page failed to load).

glossary.plainLanguage: A mercenary hit squad that does SERN's dirty work, taking orders from a commander called 'FB'.
glossary.details: Separate from SERN but working for it. Any Rounder who finds an IBN 5100 is eliminated afterward. On the Alpha line they raid the Lab and kill Mayuri.

glossary.plainLanguage: The codename of the Rounders' commander, who sends Moeka her orders by text.
glossary.details: Stands for Ferdinand Braun.

reveals.text: FB is Yugo Tennouji, the Lab's landlord ('Mr. Braun').

glossary.plainLanguage: A global communications-surveillance network that SERN uses to spy on messages, which is how it notices the Lab's D-Mails.
glossary.details: SERN captured Okabe's first D-Mail and stored it in a database only the IBN 5100 can edit.

glossary.plainLanguage: SERN's secret project to build a time machine, including human trials that turned people to gel.
glossary.details: Per one wiki: launched in secret on Feb 2, 1973; the LHC started in 2001, beginning its fourth phase; 2001-2004 tested at least 100 people ('Jellyman's Report'). The dates and numbers are single-source.

glossary.plainLanguage: An online poster claiming to be a time traveller from 2036, who warns of a SERN-ruled future and contacts Okabe.
glossary.details: On the Alpha line someone posting as Titor on '@channel' warns of a SERN dystopia, emails Okabe, and wants him to cross the 1% barrier (single wiki).

reveals.text: 'John Titor' is Suzuha Amane, Daru's daughter from 2036 (confirmed for the Alpha-line Suzuha; unclear for the Beta-line one).

glossary.plainLanguage: A real internet persona (2000-2001) who claimed to be a soldier from 2036 sent back for an IBM 5100 computer. Widely regarded as a hoax. The game borrows this legend.
glossary.details: Timeline: fax to Art Bell (July 29, 1998); IRC as 'TimeTravel_0' (Oct 14, 2000); Time Travel Institute posts from Nov 2, 2000; 'John Titor' from Jan 2001; last post late March 2001. A 2008 Italian TV investigation and investigator Mike Lynch linked it to Florida lawyer Larry Haber and his brother; they denied it. Claimed machine: in a 1967 Chevrolet Corvette (Wikipedia; a fan wiki says Camaro).

glossary.plainLanguage: Okabe's self-styled 'lab': a rented room in Akihabara above a CRT TV shop, where he and his friends build odd gadgets.
glossary.details: Rented from Yugo Tennouji above the Braun Tube Workshop.

glossary.plainLanguage: Each Lab member gets a number in the order they joined, starting with Okabe as 001.
glossary.details: 001 Okabe, 002 Mayuri, 003 Daru, 005 Moeka, 007 Faris, 008 Suzuha are stated; 004 Kurisu and 006 Luka follow from join order only; 010 Kagari is single-source; 009 and 011 are unknown. Yuki appears as a member only in promotional material.

glossary.plainLanguage: A real building in Akihabara where the story begins on July 28, 2010, at Dr. Nakabachi's press conference.
glossary.details: A satellite-like object is on its roof when Okabe arrives (VN). Akihabara and Radio Kaikan are real locations.

reveals.text: The 'satellite' is Suzuha's time machine, wedged between the top floor and the roof because her arrival coordinates were slightly off.

glossary.plainLanguage: Tokyo's electronics and otaku district, where the Lab is. It is a real place.
glossary.details: Faris's D-Mail causes a line where moe/otaku culture never reaches Akihabara.

glossary.plainLanguage: The CRT TV shop directly below the Lab, run by Okabe's landlord Yugo ('Mr. Braun'), where Suzuha works part-time.
The shrine where Luka works, which holds an IBN 5100 on some world lines.
The maid cafe where Mayuri works part-time and Faris is the star maid.
Okabe names his plans after the three Norns of Norse myth: Urd (past), Verdandi (present) and Skuld (future).
glossary.details: One blog says the anime's arcs map to them: Urd eps 1-12, Verdandi eps 13-22 (undoing D-Mails to save Mayuri), Skuld eps 23-24. That mapping is single-source; whether the VN uses Urd/Verdandi as in-story operation names is unverified. On Wikipedia, 'Verthandi' appears only as the title of ep 22's ending theme.

glossary.plainLanguage: The final plan: save Kurisu without changing anything Okabe's past self saw, so history is 'deceived' and the Steins Gate line is reached.
glossary.details: Past Okabe must still see a 'dead' Kurisu, so the first D-Mail is still sent; the real Kurisu survives. Fandom says future Okabe designed it with Daru and Maho over about 15 years. The name is used for the anime's final arc, for the in-story plan, and by fan analysis for the video D-Mail itself.

glossary.plainLanguage: Mayuri's metal keychain toy. Swapping it for a plastic one is part of Operation Skuld.
glossary.details: Per Fandom: the metal Upa would have set off airport metal detectors, causing Nakabachi to hide the thesis elsewhere; without that alarm the thesis burned on the plane. No source confirms an Upa gel experiment.

glossary.plainLanguage: A Lab gadget: a light-up sword containing red liquid.
glossary.details: Sources disagree on whether Okabe stages Kurisu's 'death' with his own blood, with the saber's red liquid, or both.

glossary.plainLanguage: A sign-off phrase Okabe uses at the end of his phone 'reports'. In-universe he says it has no special meaning.
glossary.details: Fan etymologies (Spanish/Latin mix, '@channel' meme, Titor's 'Tempus edax rerum') are speculation. 'Kongroo' is said to be the spelling shown on screen; 'Congroo' an early mistranslation. No creator statement was found.

glossary.plainLanguage: The VN's choice system: instead of menu choices, you decide whether to answer or ignore calls and which highlighted words to reply to in texts.
glossary.details: Steins;Gate 0 uses phone choices too (phone on/off; answering or ignoring Amadeus).

glossary.plainLanguage: A technique for reading memories out of the brain as data, used both by the Time Leap Machine and by the Amadeus AI.
glossary.details: Developed at Viktor Chondria University in the 1990s per Fandom; Amadeus is built on Kurisu's 'Visual Rebuilding' thesis.

glossary.plainLanguage: The American university where Kurisu, Maho and Leskinen work at the Brain Science Institute.
An AI system that stores a person's memories and can talk like them. In Steins;Gate 0, an Amadeus built from Kurisu's memories becomes Okabe's conversation partner.
glossary.details: Built at Viktor Chondria University on Kurisu's Visual Rebuilding thesis, led by Alexis Leskinen and Maho Hiyajo; named after Mozart. It becomes a target because it preserves Kurisu's time-machine theory; a D-RINE erases it (anime ep 22).

glossary.plainLanguage: A D-Mail sent through a chat app (RINE) instead of plain text messaging, developed by Daru on Beta lines so SERN cannot trace it via ECHELON.
glossary.details: Used in Steins;Gate 0, e.g. to erase Amadeus (anime ep 22). A guidebook reportedly admits no specific rule decides which world line receives a D-RINE.

glossary.plainLanguage: In Steins;Gate 0, people around the world start remembering or dreaming of other world lines: a weak, widespread form of Reading Steiner.
glossary.details: From August 2010 on the Beta line, first in America then Japan; treated as 'encephalitis cases'. On 1.382733% the mass effect is called 'President's Disease' (people remember a different Russian president). The wiki says Nakase and Okabe both have 'President Syndrome'.

glossary.plainLanguage: The resistance group in the future that Suzuha belongs to and that takes in the orphan Kagari.
glossary.details: Listed for both the Alpha and Beta lines (single wiki). Beta membership per a stub flagged 'inconsistent sources' includes Okabe, Daru, Suzuha, Yuki, Maho, Luka, Faris, Kagari and others; Mayuri only in the VN/manga and 'Amadeus Kurisu' only in the anime. Fandom credits 'countless attempts' by the Lab or Valkyrie for reaching Steins Gate.

glossary.plainLanguage: A Steins;Gate 0 mission in which Suzuha and Mayuri travel back to August 21, 2010 to restore Okabe's will to try again.
glossary.details: Its details reach Suzuha via a D-Mail from Daru (anime ep 17). Anime ep 23 is titled 'Arc-light of the Point at Infinity'. The Arc Light drama CD/manga share the S;G 0 line value 1.129848%.

glossary.plainLanguage: 'Altair' appears in the VN route 'Vega and Altair' and anime episode titles. One wiki uses 'Operation Altair' for rescuing Suzuha and Mayuri from 18,000 BC; it is not verified as an in-story operation name.
A Steins;Gate 0 operation in which a D-RINE is sent to the past.
glossary.details: Dated December 2011 by a single wiki, possibly a typo for 2010.

glossary.plainLanguage: Rival intelligence groups in Steins;Gate 0 fighting over Kurisu's time-travel research, alongside Russia.
glossary.details: Leskinen secretly works for Stratfor (also given as Strategic Focus / Stratfoc); TV Tropes says Judy Reyes is a DURPA agent. A DURPA helicopter missile destroys Suzuha's time machine (anime ep 19).

glossary.plainLanguage: A Steins;Gate 0 VN bad ending in which Okabe falls into despair.
glossary.details: Reached with the phone ON at Closed Epigraph (Dec 15) and answering Amadeus at Pandora's Box (Jan 23); world line 1.129954% then 1.143688%.

glossary.plainLanguage: Spin-off stories add more fields beyond Alpha and Beta. They are not part of the core VN/anime/Steins;Gate 0 story.
glossary.details: Gamma (2.x): SERN dystopia with Okabe as dictator (Hyde of the Dark Dimension). Delta (3.x): seemingly peaceful (My Darling's Embrace, Linear Bounded Phenogram). Epsilon (4.x): made for Linear Bounded Phenogram. Omega (negative values): the Lab never forms. Chi: 1.048599 and 1.049326 (Robotics;Notes Revival Legacy). Steins;Gate Re:Boot's 'Gamma Worldline' route is reported separately; its relation to the spin-off Gamma field is not stated.

mechanics.title: D-Mail: texting the past
mechanics.oneLiner: A short text sent through the Lab's phone-microwave arrives in the past. If it changes what someone does, the whole world line shifts.

steps.caption: Call the phone wired into the microwave, press '#', and enter a time.
steps.visualHint: Phone icon rings; keypad '#' lights; microwave timer digits appear.

steps.caption: The big CRT TV downstairs must be on. It is the 'lifter' that feeds the effect.
steps.visualHint: Cutaway of the building: CRT below glows; a dashed energy line climbs to the microwave.

steps.caption: The microwave makes tiny spinning black holes. Data can slip through; solid things come back as gel.
steps.visualHint: A small ring-shaped vortex forms; a banana icon enters and exits as a green blob.

steps.caption: Only about 36 bytes fit, split into three 12-byte pieces. Extra text is lost.
steps.visualHint: Message bar chops into three equal packets; overflow letters fade out.

steps.caption: The timer sets how far back the text goes, in one-hour steps.
steps.visualHint: Packets fly left along a calendar strip and land on a chosen hour.

steps.caption: If the text changes a past decision, history is rebuilt and the world line's number changes.
steps.visualHint: The calendar strip 'reweaves'; the Nixie readout rolls to a new value.

steps.caption: Everyone's memories now match the new history, except Okabe's.
steps.visualHint: Figures' memory tapes rewind and rewrite in a new colour; Okabe's tape is copied over unchanged.

mechanics.whatDoesNotTravel: People, objects (they turn to gel) and memories.

limits.text: Target time set in one-hour steps; no formula for converting the timer to hours is given.
No stated maximum reach; canon sends reach January 1993 and April 3, 2000.
Works only while the CRT 'lifter' is on.

commonMisconceptions.claim: The lottery mail was the first D-Mail.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The first was the accidental July 28 text to Daru; the lottery mail was the first deliberate change.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Undoing a D-Mail restores the exact old world line.
commonMisconceptions.correction: It lands on a nearby but different value (0.409420 vs 0.409431; 0.571024 vs 0.571046).

commonMisconceptions.claim: Any message changes the world line.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Only changes big enough to move the meter's six decimals trigger a visible shift and Reading Steiner.

mechanics.title: Time leap: sending your memories back
mechanics.oneLiner: Only memories travel, up to 48 hours back, into your own past self. The body stays put.

steps.caption: A headset reads the leaper's memories and turns them into data.
steps.visualHint: Head silhouette; glowing threads stream out into a data cube.

steps.caption: The data goes to SERN's hacked collider, where a mini black hole squeezes it down to D-Mail size.
steps.visualHint: Cube flies to a ring-shaped collider and compresses to a tiny packet.

steps.caption: The packet is pushed through the phone-microwave to the leaper's own phone, up to 48 hours earlier.
steps.visualHint: Packet zips left along the calendar strip, at most two day-tiles.

steps.caption: The past self must answer and hold the phone to their ear; the memories are written into their brain.
steps.visualHint: Past-self silhouette lifts phone; threads flow into the head; second silhouette fades.

steps.caption: The leap itself does not move the world line. Only what the leaper then does differently can.
steps.visualHint: Nixie readout stays frozen during the jump; a note badge says INTERPRETATION.

mechanics.whatDoesNotTravel: The body; per one wiki, also not 'consciousness or personality'.

limits.text: 48 hours is the safe maximum; a longer jump risks brain damage because the brain changes over time.
The past self's phone must be on, with them, and answered.
Steins;Gate 0: Maho extends the range to two weeks.

commonMisconceptions.correction: It is the stated safe limit; Steins;Gate 0 upgrades it to two weeks.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A time leap changes the world line.
commonMisconceptions.correction: No reference source says a leap alone shifts divergence; leaping 'combined with D-Mails' lets you move between lines.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Time leaping sends your body back.

mechanics.title: Reading Steiner: the one who remembers
mechanics.oneLiner: When the world line changes, everyone's memories rewrite themselves to fit the new history. Okabe's don't.

steps.caption: A D-Mail (or a big enough change in the present) moves the world to a new line.
steps.visualHint: Nixie digits roll.

steps.caption: The world is 'reconstructed': physical reality and memories become the new line's.
steps.visualHint: Scene desaturates, twists, and re-forms with small differences.

steps.caption: Okabe's memories are copied onto the new line, overwriting the new-line Okabe from the moment the D-Mail was sent.
steps.visualHint: Okabe's memory tape slides across from the old scene into the new one.

steps.caption: He feels vertigo; the world goes monochrome and blurry for a few seconds.
steps.visualHint: Brief monochrome swirl around Okabe's silhouette only.

steps.caption: It does not fire for changes too small to move the meter, for physical time travellers, or for time leaps.
steps.visualHint: Three crossed-out mini icons.

steps.caption: Others sometimes catch faint echoes: deja vu or dreams.
steps.visualHint: Faint ghost frames flicker over other figures.

mechanics.whatTravels: Okabe's memories (copied onto the new line).
mechanics.whatDoesNotTravel: Everyone else's memories (rewritten to the new history).

limits.text: Its origin is never explained; a childhood fever around age 8 is implied.

commonMisconceptions.correction: Others (Mayuri, Luka, Faris, Kurisu, Nakase, Amadeus) show partial recall; Okabe's is uniquely strong and consistent.

mechanics.title: Attractor fields and convergence
mechanics.oneLiner: World lines bundle into families that all reach the same fate. Small changes alter when and how, not whether.

steps.caption: Many world lines bundle into a few 'fields'.
steps.visualHint: Many thin threads braid into a few ropes (metaphor; INTERPRETATION).

steps.caption: Each field has a fixed outcome. Alpha (0.x%): Mayuri dies in August 2010; SERN rules by 2036. Beta (1.x%): Kurisu dies July 28, 2010; World War III follows.
steps.visualHint: Each rope ties into one knot labelled with its outcome.

steps.caption: Inside a field, changes shift the time or method but not the outcome.
steps.visualHint: Thread hops between neighbours but still hits the knot; date label slides a day later.

steps.caption: To escape, divergence must cross about 1%: Okabe undoes every D-Mail and erases the first.
steps.visualHint: Thread jumps across the 1% gap from one rope to the other.

steps.caption: Steins Gate (1.048596%) avoids both knots by keeping what past-Okabe saw while changing the hidden facts.
steps.visualHint: A separate highlighted thread runs between the two ropes.

mechanics.whatTravels: n/a (this is a rule, not a device).

limits.text: No source explains why field boundaries fall on whole percentages; the first digit is only a rule of thumb.

commonMisconceptions.claim: You need to move more than 4%.
commonMisconceptions.correction: A blog figure contradicted by every other source; the barrier is 1%.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Mayuri always dies on the same date on every Alpha line.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The outcome converges; the date shifts (a day later in anime ep 17).

commonMisconceptions.claim: Steins Gate is just another Beta line.
commonMisconceptions.correction: It is neither an ordinary Alpha nor Beta line; whether it is its own field is a wording dispute.

mechanics.title: The Divergence Meter
mechanics.oneLiner: A Nixie-tube readout of the current world line's number, which only someone who remembers the old value can use.

steps.caption: Nixie tubes show the divergence to six decimal places.
steps.visualHint: Eight glowing Nixie digits, warm orange.

steps.caption: When the world line shifts, the reading changes.
steps.visualHint: Digits roll like a slot machine and settle.

steps.caption: Only Okabe notices, because everyone else's memory of the old reading is rewritten.
steps.visualHint: Two observers: one sees old/new values side by side, the other sees only the new.

steps.caption: The leading digit usually names the field (0.x Alpha, 1.x Beta), with exceptions.
steps.visualHint: Leading digit highlights; band label appears.

steps.caption: It ignores changes past the sixth decimal and cannot show negative numbers (the first digit goes blank).
steps.visualHint: Seventh digit flickers but never displays; a blank first tube.

limits.text: What the number is measured against is not firmly defined.

commonMisconceptions.correction: No source ties it to 2025; the invention year is given as 2021 or 'some years before 2020'.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Each line has one fixed reading forever.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Later spin-offs show two superposed values.

mechanics.title: Suzuha's time machine
mechanics.oneLiner: The only way a body travels: a 2036 machine that controls Kerr black holes, burns fuel, and nudges the divergence each trip.

steps.caption: It calculates gravity fields and coordinates and controls Kerr black holes.
steps.visualHint: Ring-shaped vortex inside a capsule outline.

steps.caption: Each trip uses fuel from a car-battery-sized cell; unused for a year, it stops working.
steps.visualHint: Battery gauge drains one notch per jump.

steps.caption: Travellers are not 'reconstructed', so they keep their memories when the line changes.
steps.visualHint: Traveller silhouette stays solid while the world around reweaves.

steps.caption: Every trip shifts the divergence slightly: two Beta trips went 1.130205 -> 1.130209 -> 1.130212.
steps.visualHint: Nixie digits tick up in the last places.

steps.caption: The Alpha-line machine is one-way: it can only go further into the past.
steps.visualHint: Arrow points left only; right arrow greyed.

mechanics.whatDoesNotTravel: Nothing is reconstructed for the traveller; they are exempt from memory rewriting.

limits.text: Can be damaged (the Alpha machine breaks in a thunderstorm).

commonMisconceptions.claim: It is the same kind of device as the phone-microwave.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The microwave sends only data; this machine carries bodies.

commonMisconceptions.claim: The story's John Titor is the real-world John Titor.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The game borrows the real internet legend; in-story 'Titor' is Suzuha.

sg0Branch.description: Steins;Gate 0 forks at the original's final arc: after the failed first rescue (Okabe accidentally stabs Kurisu), Okabe returns to Aug 21, 2010 broken and refuses a second attempt. He stays on a Beta line where Mayuri lives and Kurisu is dead. Anime episode 23-beta (Dec 2, 2015) is the on-screen version of this fork.

endings.name: Anime finale (ep 23)
endings.outcome: In 2025 Okabe sends the video D-Mail, then rescues Mayuri and Suzuha from 18,000 BC. The anime merges routes into one True-End-oriented story.

animeVsVn.text: The anime is not a route-by-route adaptation: writer Chiyomaru Shikura rewrote it many times into one story accessible to non-players.

The anime removes Kagari's plastic-surgery/Yuki-decoy subplot, merges plot points from various routes into a single ending, expands Okabe's Amadeus interactions and the Alpha visit, and shows DURPA/Stratfor more.
Kagari first contacts Leskinen differently: a 1998 landline call in the anime; in the VN he finds her on the street.
The anime alone shows the 18,000 BC rescue succeeding.
The Alpha shift: a Russian nuclear time-machine test in the anime; Jan 21, 2011 for unknown reasons in the VN.
Raid on Daru's hideout: the masked biker is Moeka in the VN, Judy Reyes in the anime.
Anime-only world lines: 1.097302 (ep 8), 1.123581 (ep 22), an unnamed Beta line (ep 23).
Fan analysis: the anime is the 'final iteration' told from the viewpoint of the Okabe who records the video; critics call it a loose adaptation.

reconnection.description: Steins;Gate 0's final Okabe sends the 2025 video D-Mail. It is the static video the original Okabe received on July 28 at 12:26, which decodes after his failed first rescue and enables the successful second attempt and the Steins Gate line. So S;G 0 must happen 'before' the original's ending, and the branch loops back into it.
reconnection.arrivalDateNote: No source names the exact date the video arrives or decodes in the original.

classification.text: Officially a sequel set on a forked timeline; wiki.gg calls it an 'interquel'; fan analysis argues 'prequel'. Semantic dispute; all agree on the fork and loop-back.

endings.name: Suzuha ending
endings.outcome: Okabe relives Mayuri's last two days until he is emotionally numb; Suzuha takes him to the past to fight SERN's future. The only ending where Okabe's ultimate fate is unknown.

endings.worldLineNote: Inferred: the undo D-Mail is never sent, so the line stays 0.337187.

endings.name: Faris ending ('Isolated Jamais Vu')
endings.outcome: Okabe sends a different D-Mail so Faris's father keeps the IBN 5100; divergence passes 1% with a strange reading, his friends forget him, he lives with Faris, and Mayuri survives.
endings.howToReach: Do not send the Faris cancellation; send the alternative D-Mail instead.

endings.name: Luka ending
endings.outcome: Okabe does not cancel Luka's D-Mail; Mayuri dies of a heart attack after spending her last two days with him; Okabe and Luka stay together, and a post-credits scene shows their child.
endings.howToReach: Do not call the PhoneWave / do not cancel Luka's D-Mail.
endings.worldLineNote: Inferred from the chapter's world line; not stated.

endings.name: Mayuri ending ('Stardust Sky')
endings.outcome: Okabe realizes his feelings for Mayuri and returns to Beta; Kurisu's death stands; Okabe and Mayuri become a couple.
endings.howToReach: The default path without Kurisu flags.

endings.name: Kurisu ending ('Paradox Meltdown')
endings.outcome: Okabe and Kurisu acknowledge their feelings; her death is not prevented, Suzuha never returns, and World War III is implied.
endings.howToReach: Earn five Kurisu email flags, then ignore the 'Where are you now?' email.

endings.name: True End ('Open the Steins Gate')
endings.outcome: Operation Skuld succeeds: Steins Gate 1.048596%, both Mayuri and Kurisu live, and Okabe reunites with Kurisu. The anime adapts this route.
endings.howToReach: Reply 'Where you are' to that email (the sixth flag).

endings.outcome: The original VN has no Moeka ending, only an extra scene (ignore Kurisu's second call). Steins;Gate Re:Boot (2026) adds a Moeka route.
